title: ReFreeKV: Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression
hook: Most KV-cache pruning needs a hand-tuned budget threshold per input — pick wrong and performance craters. ReFreeKV adapts the budget on the fly instead.
key_points: KV-cache pruning usually needs a pre-set, input-specific compression threshold to stay lossless — brittle when real inputs vary in domain, length, and difficulty.
ReFreeKV adaptively allocates cache budget per input instead of relying on a fixed threshold.
Tested across 13 datasets spanning context lengths, task types, and model sizes.
Aims to preserve full-cache performance without threshold tuning per deployment.
content_html: KV-cache pruning can shrink an LLM's memory footprint almost for free — as long as you pick the right compression threshold for that specific input. Pick wrong, and quality falls off a cliff. ReFreeKV removes the threshold entirely.
extra_html: Existing KV-cache pruning methods can achieve lossless memory reduction, but they typically depend on a pre-determined, input- or domain-specific budget threshold to hit that performance. Real-world traffic spans wildly different domains, lengths, and difficulty levels with no clean boundary for choosing that threshold, so a method tuned for one setting can badly degrade on another. ReFreeKV instead adaptively adjusts how much cache budget to allocate per input, aiming to preserve full-cache performance without any threshold tuning step. Across 13 datasets covering varied context lengths, task types, and model sizes, the authors report it holds up where fixed-threshold methods falter. Code is public. Xuanfan Ni and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

related.title: KVarN: Variance-Normalized KV-Cache Quantization
related.hook: Long reasoning chains blow up the KV cache. Squeeze it to 2 bits and errors snowball over thousands of decode steps — unless you fix the token scales first.

related.title: Block-GTQ: RoPE-Aware Bit Allocation for KV-Cache Quantization
related.hook: Most KV-cache quantizers spend bits evenly across a key. Block-GTQ shows that under RoPE some frequency blocks matter far more — and gives them more bits, hitting near-fp16 quality at 2–3 bits.

related.title: The KV Cache & Continuous Batching
related.hook: Generating one token reuses every prior key and value - that growing cache is why LLM inference is memory-bound, and continuous batching is how servers fight back.

flashcards.prompt: What's the hidden weakness in most KV-cache pruning methods, per this paper?
flashcards.back_html: They need a pre-determined, input-specific budget threshold to stay lossless, which breaks down on open-domain inputs with no clear boundary for picking the threshold.

choices.text: The cache budget adapts automatically per input instead of relying on a fixed, pre-tuned threshold
No compression is applied at all
The threshold is set once and shared across all future models

flashcards.explanation_html: ReFreeKV adjusts how much cache budget to keep based on the input itself, removing the need to pre-tune a threshold for each deployment.
